title: The gemm task had no applicable dot contract on gfx938; declaring one changed nothing, and the campaign still lowers a contraction with no matrix instruction

observation:
An earlier version of this record said the author had the declaration and did not reach for it. That was wrong, and the correction is the finding.

The gemm task is fp32 -- the starter declares fp32 tensors on every target and contracts a reduce over an elementwise product. gfx938 declares dot contracts for fp16 and fp8e4m3 and for nothing else. So no admitted contract covers this workload's dtype, and a contraction written with one would have been refused: the gfx938 mma corpus case with its operands moved to fp32 assesses accepted=False. The author did not decline an available instruction; there was none available for what it was asked to compute.

That the reference bundle names both contracts is what made this look like a choice. It names what the Target declares, not what applies to the case in hand, and the two differ here by dtype alone.

The neighbouring fact is that the starter carries no tl.dot on any target, B300 included, so nothing here shows the DCU behaving differently from the incumbent -- only that the DCU cannot yet be asked to. sm_103a declares triton.dot.fp32_ieee and triton.dot.fp32_tf32; gfx938 declares no fp32 form because none has been measured on it, which is the correct state for an undeclared fact and not a defect.

Measured and closed. fp32 operands do reach this ISA's matrix unit: input_precision=ieee emits v_mmac_16x16x8_f32 and tf32 emits v_mmac_f32_16x16x8_tf32, with zero v_fma or v_pk_fma_f32 in either, and ieee is exact against a torch fp32 matmul at 64x64x64 while tf32 carries 7.177e-04 relative error -- which is the reduced mantissa, and the reason they are two contracts and not one. That question had to be asked: a contract naming a matrix instruction the hardware does not run for this dtype would have been worse than declaring none.

Both are now declared, and both of their analyses were already in place because the CUDA targets declare the same two contracts -- so nothing needed the treatment F-2026-09-17-008 insists on, which is the first time that has been true here. The same fp32 contraction that assessed accepted=False an hour earlier now lowers.

The declaration did not change the behaviour, and that is the result.

This record has now been wrong in both directions. It first said the author had the capability and declined it; I corrected that to say the author could not have used it, because the task is fp32 and no fp32 contract existed. The second statement was true and turned out not to be the explanation. With triton.dot.fp32_ieee and triton.dot.fp32_tf32 declared, measured on the device, and a Corpus case lowering to tl.dot at fp32, gemm ran again and produced a candidate with no matrix instruction anywhere and a confirmed latency identical to six decimal places -- 0.409279 ms, the same number as before the contracts existed.

So the missing contract was a real blocker and not the operative one. Removing it was necessary to ask the question and did not answer it. What remains is the authoring environment: the gemm starter is a reduce over an elementwise product on every target, B300 included, and nothing an author is shown for this task uses a matrix instruction. That is now the only explanation still standing, and it is testable -- a starter or Corpus example that uses the declared contract would settle it -- but it changes the task statement, which S5 fixes as part of the treatment.
proposed_change:
Do not widen anything to force it; the candidate is correct and the run adherent. The open question is narrower than it was: with the contract available and unused, the remaining candidate explanation is that nothing in the authoring environment shows a contraction on this target using one.

Testing that means changing the starter or adding a worked Corpus example, which changes the treatment: campaigns before and after are not matched, and that boundary has to be recorded rather than absorbed. It is worth doing deliberately, because the alternative is a target that declares a matrix unit no campaign ever reaches.

What this record should not be read as: evidence that the model cannot use mma. One task, one shape, two runs. The contracts are declared and gate-covered now, so the next campaign that wants one is not blocked by the Compiler.
verified_by: the fp32 probe on a BW1101 -- v_mmac_16x16x8_f32 for ieee with max_abs_error 0, v_mmac_f32_16x16x8_tf32 for tf32 at 7.177e-04 relative, no v_fma in either -- and Corpus case gfx938-gemm-bias-mma-fp32-accepted, which lowers to tl.dot(..., input_precision="ieee")
